terms.name: base
terms.meaning: The robot's base origin: the one body point a hallway scenario tracks. Its position is read at each recorded sample.
terms.frame: The world frame, in meters: x and y along the floor, z up from the floor. Lateral distance is measured from the route centerline: the line y = 0 in the straight hallway, the route polyline in the corner worlds.
terms.units: meters for position, seconds for sample time

nominal.rule: The base position has no per-robot nominal. A scenario states places (exit, centerline) and numbers, not a nominal.

sources: livingproof-evaluator-scenario checks.py: exit crossing and distance from the route, from the base point of each trace sample (x, y)
robot-capability-specs walk-hallway README: places, not axes (the body point is the base origin)

terms.name: base height
terms.meaning: How high the base origin is above the floor. The hallway grades its lowest value over the trial.
terms.frame: The world frame, measured up from the floor (z = 0).

nominal.rule: The fall threshold is the absolute fall_height that the walk-hallway spec grades against: the configuration profile's locomotion.fall_base_height, in meters (0.5 m for the G1). The nominal, the per-robot nominal_base_height, is the measured standing base height in meters (0.78 m for the G1 stock configuration). It is reference data only and is not the grading threshold. A threshold stated as a ratio of nominal would be a separate spec change.

sources: examples/scenario/graded/request.json: step stay-upright (the step text names the fall height, the absolute fall_height the spec grades)
livingproof-evaluator-scenario checks.py: fail_less grades min_base_height against fall_height, which is the manifest's fall_base_height

terms.name: body contact
terms.meaning: Contact between the robot body and a named environment surface. The scenario names the surface, for example a hallway wall. Each contact has its surface, a start time, an end time and a depth: how far the farthest collision part reaches past the surface's inner face, the largest while the contact lasts. That depth is an intrusion, not a penetration depth.
terms.frame: The scenario world: the world names each surface (the hallway has wall-left and wall-right) and times run from the start of the trial.
terms.units: depth in meters, start and end in seconds

nominal.rule: Body contact has no per-robot nominal. The hallway rule is that no contact with a hallway wall is recorded, a limit of zero.

sources: examples/binding/merged/unitree-g1-stock-livingproof-sim-mujoco.json: body_contact is listed as unbound, as the recording has no contact channel yet
livingproof-evaluator-scenario checks.py: fail_not_empty reads wall_contacts, the hallway metric for this term
robot-capability-specs walk-hallway README: wall_contacts must be empty

metrics.maps: The hallway evaluator's wall_contacts metric is the list of body_contact events with hallway walls, each {wall, start, end, depth}. The hallway passes when the list is empty.
